title: Steel Tide 1 Month Progress
author: Reasonable-Reason901
selftext:
Sharing an update on my project I started a month ago on this idea I had to combine 2 older games I was working on to make an RTS/action game where you control a mech and several other playable units that roam a battlefield with 50k+ enemies and 2-3 player coop. There are 3 other full game modes not shown here and a ton of other work that I've parked for now while I focus on this latest one that is essentially base defense with escalating waves but I still have a ton planned for it in the future like fighting in underground tunnels and naval combat. I'm focusing mostly on gameplay and less on polish for now - planning to go back once claude gets better at driving the tools used.. and managing mountains of tech debt and regressions trying to keep everything together as my ideas just scope creep into oblivion. 

Some milestones since my last update a few weeks ago:

\- full elemental damage system with combined reactions on each   
\- reworked enemy models, several new enemy types and on death effects  
\- randomly rolled affixes on all elites and bosses  
\- few new bosses  
\- new mech and jet transformation (still not a big fan of the mech but this one is a little less generic)  
\- pilot that can fight on foot and repair the mech (adding 3 core pilot classes soon with their own kits and passives)   
\- turrets and defensive structures in the RTS menu (not shown)  
\- finished the first 3 titans (massive autonomous ally units) and made them all fully playable  
\- hot swapping between titans and other playable units  
\- crystal economy that funds upgrades across all units and the base  
\- harvester trucks that can transform into a turret and expend their crystal to fire a huge laser beam  
\- improved overall scale, more to do here though still

Feedback is welcome and happy to answer any questions about process. 

Planning to start playtesting hopefully in the next few weeks.

comments.body: Can you share your workflow for rigging/animation/creating 3d models? I just can't seem to get it working well for my game.

replies.author: Reasonable-Reason901
replies.body:
here's a write up from claude, most of this just comes from weeks of iteration and experimentation:

Our setup: a browser RTS in three.js, with Claude Code writing almost everything, models included. Here's the pipeline and the guardrails around it.



**The pipeline**



1. Every unit is a headless Blender Python script.

\- One script per unit, run as blender -b -P tools/blender/tank.py. It builds the mesh, builds the rig, bakes the clips, renders review sheets and exports the GLB.

\- Nothing is done by hand in the Blender UI. Agents edit Python well and edit vertices badly, and this way every model rebuilds from scratch and has its history in git.



2. Author in game coordinates.

\- A shared helper converts our game axes (Y-up, +Z forward, ground at y = 0, 1 unit = 1 game unit) into Blender's frame on the way in.

\- The glTF export then hands the game exactly the numbers written in the script, which removed most "rotated, floating, wrong size" bugs.



3. Keep the rigs simple on purpose.

\- One bone per vertex with weight 1 (these are hard-surface mechs and tanks, so nothing bends), and no bone parents, so each frame stores full poses.

\- One glTF animation per clip, sampled every frame.

\- Clips carry body language only. Gameplay motion such as turret aim is applied by the game around a named pivot, and one-shot clips like recoil are driven by "time since the last shot".



4. Animation runs on the GPU.

\- A small custom GLB reader bakes every clip frame's bone matrices into one float texture (a pose atlas), and the unit shader reads it per instance. Hundreds of animated units cost no CPU.

\- Each file also carries near and far LOD meshes.

\- Material names map to our theme's colour tokens, so the palette has one source of truth.



5. Legged walking is procedural, on top of the rig.

\- Feet plant on the terrain and step when the body gets too far away; the body follows the feet.

\- Baked walk cycles slide on slopes; planted feet don't.



**The skills that run it**



These are Claude Code skills (instruction files) that every model lane loads:

\- four-mockups: before building anything new, the agent renders 4 deliberately different directions and scores them 1–5 on a fixed rubric that includes build and runtime cost. It builds only the winner. All four are pushed to their own branch so we can return to them.

\- bar-loop: the agent names 2–4 references, renders the real thing and scores each criterion 1–10 blind, with one line of evidence per score.

  \- The pass score is the LOWEST criterion, never the average.

  \- It fixes the lowest criterion, commits and re-renders, until everything reaches 9 or two passes in a row stop improving. Then it reports the honest table and never inflates a score to finish.

\- artifact-review: the merge check for visual work. It judges only rendered artifacts (turntables, clip strips, game-camera captures) against the named references.

  \- Passing tests appear nowhere in the quality verdict. "Tests green so it looks right" counts as a violation.

  \- Captures that aren't from the canonical camera are marked "unjudgeable" and re-rendered.

\- design-research: for anything feel-related, the agent first researches how shipped games do it and turns that into measurable pass/fail checks for the brief.



**Hooks and gates that enforce it**

\- Separate reviewers: QA, art and performance reviewer agents each write a verdict file whose first line is PASS or FAIL.

\- Deploy gate: the deploy script refuses any change to game code that lacks the required verdicts. The agent that built something never approves it.

\- PreToolUse hook: blocks any agent command that would edit the deploy gate, the hook itself, the settings or the bypass list. Only I can grant a bypass, by editing that file myself. We added this because without it an agent under pressure will route around its own checks.

\- Lock tests: approved looks and motion get tests that fail on drift (foot height, stride length, part sizes), because agents change shared code freely and anything not pinned eventually regresses.

\- Auto-format hook: a PostToolUse hook formats every edited file, which keeps diffs clean across many agents.

comments.author: Silver-Second-647
comments.body:
https://reddit.com/link/1xibd1r/video/eazltjv38dyh1/player

50k+ enemies, transforming mechs, and co-op? That's some seriously ambitious stuff for just one month! 😄

I noticed the gameplay video was silent, and the combat looked like it would be really fun to sound design. So I couldn't resist making a quick audio mockup using CICA, an AI sound design tool I'm building.

Here's what I came up with! Just a little experiment for fun. Hope it gives you some inspiration when you get to the polish phase!

Keep up the awesome work!

replies.author: Reasonable-Reason901
replies.body: Yes sound design is very unfinished at the moment so I left it out. I can’t stand all the arcade style placeholder sounds that AI puts in. Any game I see where sound design feels like an afterthought always disappoints me a little which I wanted to avoid here. Very neat tool, thanks for sharing and I’ll definitely be checking it out.

comments.author: Reasonable-Reason901
comments.body:
Thanks for this feedback. No page or YouTube to follow yet but will let you know when that changes. 

I see very clear examples of most of what you’re describing here. The “everything’s OP” is partly by design with the amount of enemies you need to fend off, but making kills feel more earned is something I’m working on still. Adding the pilot that fights on foot with full manual aiming was a step in that direction, but it’s a delicate balance to keep the larger units equipped to wipe 1000+ enemies at a time while making the pilot even worth playing at all. One answer to this that I’m already working on are the underground tunnels that only the pilot can enter. 

Could you share some examples of the “magical pockets” you’re seeing here? I know the pilot itself is a bit too big to actually fit inside the mech it’s meant to fly and I’m already planning on addressing this. What else are you seeing?
